title: How to Choose Sunglasses for Your Face Shape
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: The right sunglasses can transform your look. Here's the definitive guide to matching frames with your face shape — no guesswork needed.
content:
Why Face Shape Matters

Your face is the canvas — your sunglasses are the frame. The right pairing creates harmony; the wrong one can overpower your features. Understanding your face shape is the fastest way to shortcut your next sunglasses purchase.

Identify Your Face Shape

Pull your hair back and look straight into a mirror. Trace the outline of your face with a washable marker or just observe. Most faces fall into one of five categories:

  • Oval: Forehead slightly wider than jaw, cheekbones are the widest part, face gradually narrows at chin.
  • Round: Equal width and length, soft curved jawline, full cheeks.
  • Square: Strong jaw and forehead of similar width, angular features.
  • Heart: Wide forehead tapering to a narrow, often pointed chin.
  • Diamond: Narrow forehead and jawline with wide cheekbones.

The Best Frames for Each Shape

Oval faces are the lucky ones — almost every frame style works. Experiment freely with aviators, wayfarers, round frames, and oversized styles. The one thing to avoid: frames narrower than the widest part of your face.

Round faces benefit from angular frames that add definition. Square, rectangular, or geometric shapes create contrast against soft curves. Avoid perfectly round frames — they emphasise the roundness. Wayfarers and square frames from our Ray-Ban collection work beautifully.

Square faces with strong jawlines and foreheads are softened by round or oval frames. The Aviator shape is a classic choice. Oval frames and rimless styles also work well. Avoid boxy square frames that mirror your face shape.

Heart-shaped faces (wider at the forehead, narrower at the chin) are balanced by frames that are wider at the bottom — aviators, low-set bridges, and light-coloured or rimless frames draw attention away from the broad forehead.

Diamond faces with prominent cheekbones suit oval and rimless frames. Cat-eye shapes can also work well by drawing attention upward to the forehead.

Beyond Shape: Other Factors

Face shape is a starting point, not a rule. Your skin tone, personal style, and how you plan to use the sunglasses also matter. Someone who cycles to work needs different features than someone who wears sunglasses primarily as a fashion accessory.

title: Ray-Ban vs Oakley: Which Brand is Right for You?
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: Two iconic brands, two very different philosophies. We break down the key differences in style, technology, and value to help you decide.
content:
Two Legends, Two Worlds

Ray-Ban and Oakley are both owned by EssilorLuxottica — the world's largest eyewear company — yet they couldn't be more different in identity. Ray-Ban is fashion and cultural legacy; Oakley is engineering and athletic performance. Understanding this core difference makes choosing between them straightforward.

Ray-Ban: Style and Heritage Since 1937

Created for US Army Air Corps pilots in 1937, Ray-Ban frames have been worn by Steve McQueen, Bob Dylan, Michael Jackson, and countless others. The Aviator, Wayfarer, Clubmaster, and Round frames have achieved iconic status that transcends generations and trends.

Ray-Ban lenses (G-15 classic green, B-15 brown) are made from premium glass with excellent optical clarity. Their UV protection is genuine. Frame construction is solid, and many styles last 5-10 years with proper care. They look equally at home at a business meeting, at the beach, or on a bike.

Oakley: Performance Engineering Since 1975

Founded by motocross enthusiast Jim Jannard, Oakley was built from the ground up for sport. Their proprietary technologies include PRIZM lenses (which enhance contrast for specific environments — road cycling, cricket, golf), Unobtainium nose pads and earsocks that grip more when wet, and Impact Resistance XL frames designed to meet ANSI Z87.1 safety standards.

If you're cycling on Bangalore's roads at 6am, playing cricket on weekends, or spending full days outdoors, Oakley's engineering advantages are meaningful. The PRIZM Road lenses, for example, make road imperfections and hazards visually pop in a way standard lenses don't.

Price Comparison

At Naina Optics, Ray-Ban frames typically range from ₹6,000 to ₹15,000 depending on the model and lens type. Oakley ranges from ₹10,000 to ₹20,000+ for their performance lines. Both are genuine products with manufacturer warranties.

The Verdict

Choose Ray-Ban if you want versatile, stylish eyewear that works in social, professional, and casual settings. Choose Oakley if you're an athlete or spend significant time outdoors and want technology that actively improves visual performance. Many of our customers own one of each — a pair of Aviators for everyday use, and a Radar EV for weekend rides.

title: Polarized vs Non-Polarized Lenses: Which is Better?
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: Polarization adds ₹500–2,000 to the price of sunglasses. Is the upgrade worth it? We explain the science and real-world difference.
content:
The Science of Glare

When sunlight hits a flat surface — a road, a car bonnet, a lake, a glass building — it reflects back towards your eyes in a concentrated horizontal wave. This is glare. It causes squinting, eye fatigue, and in traffic, can be genuinely dangerous.

How Polarized Lenses Work

A polarized lens contains a laminated filter oriented vertically. It only allows vertically-oriented light waves to pass through — and since reflected glare travels horizontally, it's blocked almost entirely. The result: dramatically improved visual clarity, reduced eye strain, and truer colour perception without the washed-out brightness of ordinary tinted lenses.

When Polarization Makes a Difference

Driving: Bangalore traffic means constant reflections from other vehicles, wet roads, and glass buildings. Polarized lenses reduce fatigue on long drives significantly. Many of our customers report they can drive for two hours with polarized lenses without the headache they'd normally get.

Outdoor activities: Cycling, cricket, hiking, or even walking in Cubbon Park — polarized lenses keep you comfortable for longer in bright conditions.

Water activities: For fishing or boating, polarized lenses are essential — you can actually see into the water rather than seeing a mirror of the sky.

When Polarization is Not Ideal

Skiing (polarized lenses can make ice patches harder to spot). Reading LCD screens (the polarization filter can make screens appear dark at certain angles — relevant for ATM screens and some car instrument panels). Generally, these are minor inconveniences rather than real problems for most users.

The Cost of Polarization

At Naina Optics, polarized lenses typically add ₹500–2,000 to the frame price, depending on the brand and lens quality. For everyday outdoor use in Bangalore, we almost always recommend the upgrade. Polaroid's entire range is polarized by definition — it's in the brand name. Ray-Ban and Oakley both offer polarized variants of their popular models.

title: Best Sunglasses for Bangalore's Climate and Lifestyle
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: Bangalore's unique mix of intense UV, monsoon rains, and dusty roads demands specific features in sunglasses. Here's what to look for.
content:
Bangalore's UV Reality

Sitting at 920 metres above sea level, Bangalore receives more UV radiation than cities at lower altitudes. The UV index regularly hits 8–10 (Very High) from March through October. This makes quality UV protection not just a comfort feature but a genuine health necessity.

The Monsoon Factor

From June through September, Bangalore experiences heavy, unpredictable rain. Sunglasses need to handle moisture — look for water-repellent lens coatings and frames that won't corrode or warp. Polaroid's TR90 frames and Ray-Ban's acetate frames handle the monsoon well. Avoid metal frames without proper coating if you cycle or commute by bike during the rains.

Dust and Air Quality

Bangalore's rapid growth means significant dust on many roads. Wrap-around styles like the Oakley Radar EV offer more peripheral coverage that keeps dust out. For two-wheeler commuters, a wrap-around style with Unobtainium grip (Oakley's non-slip material) prevents the glasses from sliding off in traffic.

Our Recommendations for Bangalore

Two-wheeler commuters: Oakley Radar EV or Oakley Half Jacket — wrap-around protection, PRIZM Road lenses for traffic clarity, secure fit.

Office professionals: Ray-Ban Aviator or Clubmaster — professional enough for office settings, excellent UV protection for the commute.

Outdoor enthusiasts: Polaroid Premium Sport — polarized lenses for weekend hikes or cycling in Nandi Hills, affordable and durable.

Fashion-forward buyers: Ray-Ban Round or Oversized frames — Bangalore's young professional crowd sets trends, and these frames stand out while offering genuine protection.

title: Contact Lens Care: The Complete Beginner's Guide
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: Starting with contact lenses can feel daunting. This step-by-step guide covers everything from insertion to storage to when to see a doctor.
content:
Before You Start: See an Eye Specialist

Contact lenses are medical devices. Before buying your first pair, you need a proper contact lens fitting (different from a spectacle prescription) from an eye care professional. This determines the base curve and diameter that fits your eye, and confirms that contact lens wear is suitable for you.

The Golden Rule: Clean Hands Always

Every time you handle your lenses — inserting, removing, or cleaning — wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water. Dry them with a lint-free towel. Never touch lenses with wet hands (water introduces microorganisms). This single habit prevents the majority of contact lens-related eye infections.

Insertion Step by Step

1. Wash and dry hands. 2. Place the lens on the tip of your index finger — check it forms a bowl shape, not a flower shape (which means it's inside out). 3. Use your middle finger to pull down your lower eyelid; use your other hand to hold your upper eyelid steady. 4. Look up and place the lens gently on the lower white of your eye. 5. Look down — the lens will centre itself. 6. Blink. If it feels comfortable, you're done.

Removal

Look up. Use your middle finger to pull down the lower eyelid. With your index finger and thumb, gently pinch the lens and slide it down before lifting it off. Never try to pick a lens off from the centre of your eye — always slide it to the white first.

Cleaning Reusable Lenses

Use only fresh multi-purpose solution — never tap water, never saline alone, never old solution. Rub the lens in your palm with a few drops of solution for 20 seconds even if the bottle says 'no-rub'. Fill the clean case with fresh solution. Replace the case every 3 months.

Warning Signs

Remove lenses immediately if you experience: redness, pain, blurry vision, unusual discharge, or sensitivity to light. These can indicate infection or corneal irritation. See an eye specialist promptly — most contact lens infections respond well to treatment if caught early.

title: Blue Light Blocking Glasses: Myth, Science, or Must-Have?
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: Everyone's talking about blue light glasses. But what does the science actually say? And who really benefits from wearing them?
content:
What is Blue Light?

Blue light is a portion of the visible light spectrum (wavelengths 380–500 nanometres). The largest source of blue light is the sun — and it's the reason the sky appears blue. Digital screens (phones, computers, tablets) also emit blue light, though at significantly lower intensities than sunlight.

The Concerns

Two main concerns are discussed: digital eye strain, and disruption of circadian rhythm (sleep). The second concern has stronger scientific backing — blue light exposure in the evening suppresses melatonin production and delays sleep onset. The evidence for permanent retinal damage from screen blue light is less clear and debated among researchers.

Digital Eye Strain is Real — But Not Only About Blue Light

Digital eye strain (tired, dry, blurry eyes after prolonged screen use) is a genuine and widespread problem, particularly in Bangalore's tech-heavy workforce. However, research suggests this is primarily caused by reduced blinking, poor posture, and focusing at close distances — not specifically by blue light. Anti-reflection coatings (which reduce screen glare) may be more effective for strain than blue-light-specific filters.

Who Should Consider Blue Light Glasses

Frequent late-night screen users: If you're regularly on screens after 8pm, blue light filtering can help maintain better sleep quality. The Crizal Prevencia lens offers this alongside anti-reflection and UV protection in one lens.

Heavy screen users with eye strain: The combination of anti-reflection coating, blue light filtering, and a proper prescription (even mild) significantly reduces eye fatigue for people working 8+ hours at screens.

Our Recommendation

For most heavy screen users in Bangalore's IT and startup sectors, Crizal Prevencia lenses offer a worthwhile combination of benefits. They're not magic, but they're a meaningful part of a broader eye health strategy that includes regular breaks, proper screen distance, and annual eye tests.

title: How Often Should You Update Your Eyeglass Prescription?
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: Many people wear the wrong prescription for years without realising it. Here's how to know when it's time for a new eye test.
content:
The Standard Recommendation

Most optometrists recommend a comprehensive eye exam every 12 months for adults, and every 6–12 months for children and teenagers whose eyes are still developing. People over 40 should be particularly diligent — presbyopia (age-related near vision loss) typically begins in this decade and progresses steadily.

Signs Your Prescription Has Changed

Don't wait for your annual check if you notice these signs: blurry vision at distances that were previously clear, frequent headaches particularly around the eyes or temples, needing to squint to read or see clearly, holding reading material closer or farther than usual, or experiencing eye fatigue more than usual at the end of the day.

Why Wearing the Wrong Prescription Matters

An outdated prescription doesn't just mean blurry vision — it means your eyes are constantly compensating. This leads to eye muscle fatigue, headaches, difficulty concentrating, and can worsen symptoms of digital eye strain. Children with uncorrected vision problems may struggle academically without realising the root cause is their eyesight.

Special Cases

If you've recently been diagnosed with diabetes, high blood pressure, or are pregnant, your vision can change more rapidly and frequent monitoring is advisable. People with a family history of glaucoma, macular degeneration, or retinal conditions should also see an ophthalmologist (eye doctor, not just optometrist) annually regardless of whether their prescription seems to have changed.

title: Eye Health Tips for Bangalore's Digital Workers
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: Bengaluru is one of the world's largest tech hubs. Here's a practical guide to protecting your eyes through 8-hour screen days.
content:
The Scale of the Problem

Bangalore is home to over 1.5 million IT professionals, many spending 8–12 hours daily in front of screens. The Indian Vision Institute estimates that up to 70% of screen workers experience symptoms of digital eye strain. This is an occupational health issue that deserves the same attention as ergonomics and posture.

The 20-20-20 Rule

Every 20 minutes, look at something at least 20 feet away for at least 20 seconds. This allows your eye's focusing muscles to relax from the sustained near-focus required for screen work. Set a timer on your phone or use an app like Eye Care 20 20 20. This single habit makes a measurable difference in end-of-day eye fatigue.

Screen Setup Matters

Position your screen about arm's length from your eyes (50–70cm). The top of the screen should be at or slightly below eye level. Reduce screen brightness to match your environment — a screen that's much brighter than the surrounding room causes more strain. Tilt the screen slightly back (10–20°) to reduce glare.

Lighting in Your Workspace

Avoid working with a bright window directly behind or in front of your screen. Indirect lighting or side lighting is ideal. Overhead fluorescent lighting can cause glare — consider a desk lamp with warm light as a supplement rather than relying solely on overhead fluorescents.

Blink Consciously

We blink about 15–20 times per minute normally, but this drops to 5–7 times per minute when focused on a screen. Blinking spreads tear film across the eye and prevents dryness. Artificial tears (lubricating eye drops) can help if you experience persistent dryness. Look for preservative-free options for frequent use.

The Right Glasses for Screen Work

If you wear glasses, ensure your prescription is current. Anti-reflection coating is essential for screen workers — it eliminates the reflections from your lenses that would otherwise cause additional focusing work. Crizal Prevencia lenses offer anti-reflection, blue light filtering, and UV protection in one package and are our most popular recommendation for Bangalore's IT professionals.

title: Crizal Lens Technology Explained: What You're Actually Paying For
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: Crizal lenses cost more than standard lenses. Here's a clear breakdown of each layer of technology and whether the upgrade makes sense for you.
content:
What Crizal Is

Crizal is Essilor's premium lens treatment brand. Rather than a single coating, Crizal is a multi-layer system applied to the lens that addresses five common problems with standard eyeglass lenses: reflections, scratches, smudges, dust, and UV exposure.

Anti-Reflection Layer

Standard lenses reflect about 8% of light, creating ghost images and glare especially when driving at night or working under fluorescent lights. Crizal's anti-reflection layers reduce this to under 1%. The practical result: sharper vision, less halo effect around lights at night, and less eye fatigue. This layer alone makes a noticeable difference.

Scratch Resistance

Crizal lenses are significantly more scratch-resistant than standard AR-coated lenses. This matters because scratches degrade optical quality over time and accelerate the need for replacement. Crizal lenses come with a standard scratch warranty from Essilor.

Smudge and Water Resistance

Oils from your fingers, nose, and eyelashes smudge standard lenses easily. Crizal's surface tension properties cause oil to form droplets rather than spreading — the lens is much easier to clean and stays clean longer. Water similarly beads and slides off rather than creating blurry patches.

UV Protection: E-SPF

Essilor introduced the Eye Sun Protection Factor (E-SPF) to quantify UV protection in lenses. Crizal UV offers E-SPF 25, and Crizal Forte UV offers E-SPF 35. This means the lens provides 25x or 35x more UV protection than wearing no lens. Both the front and back surface of the lens are protected — the back surface is often forgotten, but reflected UV from behind is a real source of exposure.

Crizal Prevencia: The Blue Light Variant

Crizal Prevencia adds a specific blue light filter (445nm wavelength) on top of all the above features, making it ideal for heavy screen users. It's our most recommended lens for Bangalore's IT workforce and deserves its popularity.

Is It Worth the Price?

For daily eyeglass wearers, yes — the combination of better optics, durability, and easier maintenance extends the useful life of lenses and reduces daily frustration. For occasional wearers or those with a simple, stable prescription who rarely need glasses, standard anti-reflection coating may be sufficient.

title: Why Shopping at a Local Optical Store Matters More Than Ever
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: Online optical retail is growing fast. But there are things a neighbourhood optical store offers that no website can replicate.
content:
The Rise of Online Eyewear

Online optical retailers have made eyewear more accessible and price-competitive. Home try-on programmes, virtual frame try-on tools, and convenient delivery have genuine appeal. We don't deny this — the industry has changed, and some of these changes are positive for consumers.

What Online Cannot Replicate

The fitting: Eyeglasses that are optically perfect but physically misaligned on your face cause eye strain. The pupillary distance measurement, the vertical placement of the lens centre, the nose pad adjustment, the temple tension — these are adjustments that require a physical fitting by a trained optician. A frame that slips down your nose constantly is a frame you'll stop wearing.

The prescription interpretation: A written prescription is a starting point, not a complete lens specification. An experienced optician considers your working distance, your dominant eye, your history with progressive lenses, and dozens of other factors when recommending a lens design. This expertise is not available from a drop-down menu.

After-sales service: Adjustments, tightening, nose pad replacement, frame straightening — these are services you access continuously over the life of your glasses. Your local optician knows your frames and can service them. Online purchases often mean shipping back for repairs.

The Value of a Relationship

At Naina Optics, we have customers who have been with us since 2014. We know their prescriptions, their preferences, their workstyle. When they come in, we often remember what they last bought and can make informed recommendations. This is the kind of personalised service that creates real value over years of eyewear ownership.

title: Customer Story: Priya's Journey from Glasses to Contact Lenses
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: Priya had worn glasses for 12 years and was nervous about switching to contacts. Here's how we helped her make the transition.
content:
Twelve Years of Glasses

Priya (name changed with permission) came to us in early 2023 as a long-time spectacle wearer. A software developer at a tech company in Koramangala, she wore glasses every waking hour — from morning screen work to evening runs in Cubbon Park. She'd always been curious about contact lenses but nervous: "I've worn glasses since Class 5. The idea of touching my eye every day seemed impossible."

The Consultation

We started with a detailed conversation about her lifestyle before recommending any lens type. Her schedule: 9-10 hours at a computer, gym 3 times a week, occasional outdoor runs. Her concerns: hygiene, insertion difficulty, and whether lenses would be comfortable for long screen days.

Based on her lifestyle and moderate prescription (-2.50 both eyes), we recommended Acuvue Oasys 1-Day — daily disposables with Hydraluxe technology for screen-heavy users. The daily replacement schedule eliminates the cleaning routine that many first-timers find intimidating.

Learning Insertion

We scheduled a 30-minute insertion tutorial session. The first attempt took her 12 minutes per eye. By the end of the session, she had both lenses in comfortably. "The technique of looking up and placing it on the white part — that was the game-changer. Once I stopped trying to put it directly on my iris, it became much easier."

Three Months Later

Priya now wears contacts 4-5 days per week. She keeps her glasses for evenings and weekends. "I never thought I'd feel comfortable running with contacts — but I genuinely prefer it. No slipping, no fogging, full peripheral vision. I wish I'd done this years ago." Her advice to other nervous switchers: "The fear is worse than the reality. Give yourself one week to practice."

title: Oakley PRIZM Technology: The Science Behind Better Sports Vision
author: Satya Bharati
excerpt: Oakley's PRIZM lens technology isn't just marketing — it's based on decades of colour science research. Here's what it does and why it matters.
content:
The Problem PRIZM Solves

Standard sunglass lenses reduce all wavelengths of light uniformly. They make everything darker and more comfortable, but they don't enhance the visual information that matters for specific activities. A cyclist needs to see road texture and hazards. A cricketer needs to track a white ball against blue sky. A golfer needs to read subtle variations in green turf. Standard tints don't help with any of these specifically.

How PRIZM Works

PRIZM lenses are precision-tuned to boost specific wavelengths of the spectrum that enhance visual performance in a given environment — while suppressing the wavelengths that create visual noise. The tuning is activity-specific: PRIZM Road boosts contrast between road surfaces and objects; PRIZM Cricket emphasises the contrast between a red or white ball and the sky and turf; PRIZM Golf makes it easier to distinguish between different grass conditions.

The Research Behind It

Oakley researchers studied the specific lighting conditions, visual challenges, and performance requirements of dozens of sports. They mapped the wavelengths that create visibility challenges and the wavelengths that carry the most useful visual information. PRIZM tints are the result of translating that research into lens chemistry.

PRIZM vs Standard Polarized

These technologies can coexist — PRIZM Polarized combines the glare elimination of polarization with the contrast enhancement of PRIZM. For cycling on Bangalore's roads (strong sunlight, reflective surfaces, need to see road texture), PRIZM Road Polarized is an exceptional lens choice.

We stock a range of Oakley frames with PRIZM lens options. Our team can help you choose the right PRIZM variant based on your primary activity. Visit our Residency Road store for a consultation and to try the difference for yourself.
